label: Person
name: Ludovico Bonito
summary:
Ludovico Bonito was a Roman Catholic cardinal who played a pivotal role in the Vatican's efforts to consolidate its power during the late Middle Ages.

Born into a noble family, Bonito rose through the ranks of the clergy, becoming a key advisor to several popes before being elevated to cardinal in 1395.

As a member of the College of Cardinals, Bonito participated in numerous high-stakes conclave elections, including that of Pope Innocent VII, which took place just months before his own death in 1413.

Bonito's legacy as a master strategist and diplomat has endured for centuries, with many historians regarding him as one of the most influential figures of the papacy during this tumultuous period.

The Bonito family crest still adorns the walls of various cathedrals throughout Italy to this day.
